subject: Invert every element of a vector

messages.author: d38a9891d21d3847
messages.subject: Invert every element of a vector
parts:
Hi all,

It seems that in Stan 1.3.0 the / operator is not defined for a real and a vector, so in particular it is not possible to have:

data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=0> y[N];
...
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0> alpha;
...
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[N] mu;
...
}
model {
...
  y ~ neg_binomial(1 / alpha, 1 / (alpha * mu));
}

I was thinking to get around this I would define a vector of all 1s of the length I need in the transformed data block and divide my vector by this as follows:

data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=0> y[N];
...
}
transformed data {
  vector[N] one_vec;
  for (i in 1:N)
    one_vec[i] <- 1;
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0> alpha;
...
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[N] mu;
...
}
model {
...
  y ~ neg_binomial(1 / alpha, one_vec ./ (alpha * mu));
}


Is that all correct, or am I missing something?

Thanks,
Ted

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Invert every element of a vector
parts:
On 8/21/13 7:47 PM, Ted wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> It seems that in Stan 1.3.0 the / operator is not defined for a real and a vector, so in particular it is not possible
> to have:

Nope -- just (vector,real), which does elementwise division.

Now that you mention it, it makes sense to do it the other
way with the semantics you intended.

> |
> data {
> int<lower=1> N;
> int<lower=0> y[N];
> ...
> }
> parameters {
> real<lower=0> alpha;
> ...
> }
> transformed parameters {
> vector[N] mu;
> ...
> }
> model {
> ...
> y ~ neg_binomial(1 / alpha, 1 / (alpha * mu));
> }
> |
>
> I was thinking to get around this I would define a vector of all 1s of the length I need in the transformed data block
> and divide my vector by this as follows:
>
> |
> data {
> int<lower=1> N;
> int<lower=0> y[N];
> ...
> }
> transformed data {
> vector[N] one_vec;
> for (i in 1:N)
> one_vec[i] <- 1;
> }
> parameters {
> real<lower=0> alpha;
> ...
> }
> transformed parameters {
> vector[N] mu;
> ...
> }
> model {
> ...
> y ~ neg_binomial(1 / alpha, one_vec ./ (alpha * mu));
> }
> |
>
>
> Is that all correct, or am I missing something?

That'll work. And you can use

one_vec <- rep_vector(1,N);

instead of the loop. It'd be cleaner, but less efficient,
to just put that in the model directly:

y ~ neg_binomial(1 / alpha, rep_vector(1,N) ./ (alpha * mu));

The most efficient thing to do in Stan 1.3 (and Stan 2.0 when it
comes out) is this:

transformed parameters {
vector[N] foo;
real one_over_alpha;
one_over_alpha <- 1 / alpha;
for (n in 1:N)
foo[n] <- one_over_alpha / mu[n];
}
model {
...
y ~ neg_binomial(one_over_alpha, foo);

- Bob
